title: Where do you live?
goal: Describe where you live and move into it — and find out where the third length hides and what it is for.
bekal: use *-s*, *-st*, and *-sse* as one complete series
recognize the **short "into" form** — where the third length does its work

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Kerli korteris
dialogs.intro: Kerli invites Budi over to her apartment in the Kalamaja district of Tallinn.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Aitäh. Kas ma pean kingad ära võtma?
lines.id: Thank you. Do I have to take off my shoes?
lines.literal: thank-you. whether I must-I shoes-plural off to-take?

lines.speaker: Kerli:
lines.text: Jah, palun. Eestis võtavad kõik kingad ära.
lines.id: Yes, please. In Estonia everyone takes their shoes off.
lines.literal: yes, please. Estonia-in take-they all shoes-plural off.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Nagu Indoneesias! Kui suur su korter on?
lines.id: Just like in Indonesia! How big is your flat?
lines.literal: like Indonesia-in! how big your flat is-it?

lines.speaker: Kerli:
lines.text: Kaks tuba ja köök. Umbes viiskümmend ruutmeetrit.
lines.id: Two rooms and a kitchen. About fifty square meters.
lines.literal: two room-part and kitchen. about fifty square-meter-part.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: See on ilus. Ja väga valge.
lines.literal: it is-it pretty. and very white.

lines.speaker: Kerli:
lines.text: Aitäh. Lähme kööki, ma teen kohvi.
lines.id: Thanks. Let's go to the kitchen, I'll make coffee.
lines.literal: thank-you. go-we kitchen-to, I make-I coffee.

lines.speaker: Kerli:
lines.text: Hea kõrv! On olemas lühike vorm ja pikk vorm.
lines.id: Good ear! There is a short form and a long form.
lines.literal: good ear! is existing short form and long form.

lines.speaker: Kerli:
lines.text: Tähenduses ei ole vahet. Lühike on lihtsalt tavalisem.
lines.id: In meaning there is no difference. The short one is just more common.
lines.literal: meaning-in not is difference-part. short is-it simply more-ordinary.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Aga "kööki" ja "köögi" — need on nii sarnased!
lines.literal: but "kitchen-to" and "kitchen-of" — they-plural are-they so similar!

lines.speaker: Kerli:
lines.text: Kuula: köögi. Kööki. Kas kuuled vahet?
lines.id: Listen: köögi. Kööki. Can you hear the difference?
lines.literal: listen: kitchen-of. kitchen-to. whether hear-you difference-part?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: I think so. The second is longer.

lines.speaker: Kerli:
lines.id: Exactly. The longer one means "into", the shorter one means "of".

lines.speaker: Kerli:
lines.text: Täpselt. Nüüd sa tead eesti keele saladuse.
lines.id: Precisely. Now you know the secret of Estonian.
lines.literal: exactly. now you know-you Estonian language-of secret-of.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Siis ma pean rohkem kuulama kui lugema.
lines.id: Then I need to listen more than I read.
lines.literal: then I must-I more to-listen than to-read.

notes: ⚠️ **Taking your shoes off indoors is absolutely mandatory in Estonia**, as in much of Asia and Northern Europe. No host will say "it's fine" — they consider it obvious. If you are used to keeping shoes on at home, this is a habit you do need to learn.
**Tere tulemast!** = "Welcome!" Its literal form is odd, so learn it whole. A simple *aitäh* is enough as a reply.
**Kaks tuba** — the partitive form after a number, and notice *tuba* does not change because its partitive happens to equal the base form. Words like *muna*, *kala*, *kana* work the same way.
**Lähme kööki** = "let's go to the kitchen". *Lähme* means "let's go" and is used all the time: *lähme koju* (let's go home), *lähme sööma* (let's go eat), *lähme välja* (let's go out).

grammars.title: The inside series — in, from, into
body: You have known the first two since unit 2. This unit adds the third and completes the series.
after: All three attach to the **possessive (genitive) form**, as promised in unit 6. *Kool* → *kooli* → *koolis, koolist, koolisse*. Once more: one pair, many forms.

The surface series works in exact parallel: **-l** (on), **-lt** (off), **-le** (onto). *Laual* (on the table), *laualt* (off the table), *lauale* (onto the table). Six endings, two series, one logic.
⚠️ Which places take which series you already know from units 2 and 6: *-maa* countries, the market, streets, squares, floors, and workplaces use the surface series. The rest use the inside series.

grammars.title: ⚠️ The short "into" form — and the third length
body: The ending *-sse* is always correct and always usable. But for many everyday words, Estonians more often use a shorter form — and that short form is what carries the third length.
after: Look at the rows *kool* and *linn*: the possessive column and the "into" column are **spelled exactly the same**. The only difference is length, marked with **:** in this course and **not marked at all** in ordinary Estonian writing.
This answers a question you may have kept since the sounds page: what is the third length for? The answer: it does grammatical work. It is not sound decoration — it replaces a word ending.

⚠️ **Practical advice: when in doubt, use *-sse*.** *Koolisse*, *linnasse*, and *poesse* are all correct. The long form is never ambiguous. The short form will come on its own once your ear adjusts; don't chase it.

sections.title: Rooms and parts of the house

blocks.text: ⚠️ Notice *rõdul*, *uksel*, *aknal*, *seinal*, *põrandal*, *trepil*, *katusel* — all the **surface** series. The reason makes sense each time: you stand **on** a balcony, hang something **on** a wall, stand **on** the stairs. The inside series is for rooms you can enter.

blocks.title: Furniture you will hear often
items: ⚠️ *Külmkapp* shows Estonian's habit of gluing two words into one: *külm* (cold) + *kapp* (cupboard). Same pattern: *pesumasin* (washing machine), *tolmuimeja* (vacuum cleaner — literally "dust sucker").

blocks.title: ⚠️ Koju, kodus, kodust — the special word for "home"
items: *kodu* means home in the sense of "the place where I live", not the building. The building is *maja*.
The forms are irregular and used constantly, so learn all three now:
*kodus* — at home. *Ma olen kodus.* (I am at home.)
*koju* — homeward, to home. *Ma lähen koju.* (I'm going home.) ⚠️ Not "kodusse".
My apartment is small but cozy.
Is there an elevator in the building?

exercises.prompt: Add the ending -sse ("into") to the possessive form.
Fill in kus, kust, or kuhu.
Put the words in the right order.
